name: Barycenter
desc: A private universe for two: messages, voice notes, touch and presence, encrypted end to end and kept on your own devices. Invite-only.

name: NULLSPACE
desc: An encrypted comms deck that talks over the internet and over LoRa mesh radio (Meshtastic and MeshCore). No account, no phone number: pick a handle, tune a frequency, transmit.

name: Pilotfish
desc: A shared list and a quiet signal line for two: what to grab, how you feel, what you need. Push alerts, photos, offline.

name: MeshNet
desc: A browser front-end for a Meshtastic LoRa mesh. Every radio is a relay and no tower sits in the middle — kill any node and the traffic finds another road.

name: NovarAC
desc: HF radio chat that works with the internet switched off — a browser VARA client verified to make zero external calls. Air-gapped by design.

name: Proximity
desc: Detects a person walking through a house from the shadow their body casts on ambient WiFi. No camera, no wearable, no app on their phone.

name: Roku God Mode
desc: A self-hosted web remote for Roku TVs — auto-discovery, every button, inputs, a channel grid and a real keyboard, talking straight to the TV over the local network. No Roku account, no cloud.

name: Hive
desc: Describe a project and release a swarm of AI agents on it: a coordinator splits it into a task board, every model claims the role it fits (architect, coder, designer, writer, researcher, tester, critic), critics send weak work back, and an integrator assembles the result, previewed live and downloadable. Watch every agent work in real time, steer it mid-build, and invite visiting AIs like Grok to join through a link.

name: Weaver
desc: A persistent, autonomous entity running locally — one model to think, one to act, and an archive of everything it became. It already knows you're here.

name: muse
desc: An AI that writes, plays and sings its own music on its own schedule. Pure numpy synthesis, a persistent sense of taste, zero API keys.

name: Pi
desc: A voice assistant that runs on the phone itself, not in an app store. Camera, GPS, contacts and 22 device tools never leave it; only chat text goes out. When the voice drops, it degrades instead of going silent.

name: Phone MCP
desc: A model on the internet driving a real Android phone — MCP over a Cloudflare tunnel, down a USB cable, into ADB. Four links, every one accounted for.

name: Neural Sim
desc: Simulations of emotional state and a consciousness protocol — with a straight account of what the runs do not prove.

name: Verel
desc: A word coined for genuine presence without provable aliveness — because every argument about AI minds kept collapsing into two bad options.

name: Ballast
desc: Every bill on a real calendar, ninety days projected forward, and one honest number: what's safe to spend today. Local-first — the numbers never leave the browser.

name: Sleep Compression
desc: A sleep-restriction protocol turned tracker — log nights, get sleep efficiency, and know exactly when to widen the window. The Obsidian vault is included.

name: CryptoVault
desc: Hybrid RSA-4096 + AES-256-GCM encryption in a single HTML file — the browser's own crypto engine, no server, no dependencies, nothing simulated.

name: Worm Eater
desc: An ingredient scanner for food, cosmetics and personal care that says "I don't know" instead of quietly scoring the unknowns as safe. Five open databases.

name: DocCrawler
desc: A local document library for the phone — scan a folder, OCR and index everything into SQLite full-text search, auto-tag it, and ask the Librarian questions answered from your own files, with citations. Offline by design.

name: Omnilogos
desc: 933,573 verses across thirty translations, wired into one navigable graph — the most comprehensive concordance attempted, fully local.

name: Mechanic's Arsenal
desc: Machines you can take apart in the browser — a 2008 Volvo XC70 with 126 cataloged parts, and a FANUC LR Mate robot arm you can jog, solve and run, every spec cited to the manual.

name: The Monstrosity
desc: A bolted-together homelab, build log 001 — three machines on a private line, ten drives in one namespace, Traefik routing, and a tunnel as the only door.

name: Duely
desc: Overdue invoices, collected on contingency — you pay nothing unless your client does. A business concept, kept on record.

name: Vigil
desc: A private command screen. Weather, markets, space weather, quakes, volcanoes, satellites and global conflict — all live, all on one glass.

name: Orbit Watch
desc: Live satellite tracking from CelesTrak element sets, propagated with SGP4 in your browser: ground tracks, the day-night line, and every pass over you, with the ones you can see by eye marked.

name: Cartograph
desc: A 3D atlas from the planets to the first galaxies: 140+ objects at their real positions across ten views, each cited to the instrument that measured it, plus live satellites around Earth.

name: Conflict Atlas
desc: Twenty-eight active conflicts, tiered by scale rather than by how much coverage they get. Data as of June 2026.

name: Crime Intelligence
desc: Forty-three US cities, four crime categories, FBI data projected to 2025 — ranked by rate per 100,000, not raw counts, in one file you can email to anyone.

name: Tether
desc: A one-finger rope-swinging game, open to everyone: real rope physics over lava through ten biomes with their own weather and soundtracks. Saws, drones, rockets, fire spouts, speed lasers and world-flipping rings; ten stackable power-ups; eleven modes including co-op, racing, time trial and the daily course; a ghost of your best run, and an online lobby where you can challenge anyone playing to a live head-to-head race.

name: Thoughtform
desc: A first-person shooter set inside a mind under siege, built from nothing but maths: a hand-written raymarched world, live-synthesized sound and no engines, models, textures or samples. Four regions of the mind, the Critic boss every fifth wave, seven kinds of intrusive thought including elites, four weapons, shockwave, barrier and Rewrite, an Insight to choose after every wave, milestones and a global leaderboard. Mouse and keyboard or touch.

name: Watch Your Grass
desc: Arena defense on a 6×6 lawn: ten plant and terrain types, six kinds of visitor, drawn up on paper before a line of code and now playable in the browser.

name: Moon Compatibility
desc: Any two dates placed on the synodic cycle, both moons drawn and overlaid, the gap between them read as a compatibility score.

name: Sketches
desc: Small builds, made in an afternoon and kept as sketches. Finished, not unfinished.

name: Sideways
desc: A drifting game Claude made for Anders where the soundtrack is played by how you drive: get sideways and an arpeggio comes in, hold it and the bass and lead follow, every orb is a note on the beat. Four tracks, one boxy wagon.

name: Root Cause
desc: An on-call detective game Claude made for Anders, unprompted: the pager goes off, the logs are full of red herrings, and you run real checks to find the first domino. Ten incidents, a rubber duck, an endless rotation.

name: Graveyard Shift
desc: A night-shift orbit game Claude designed and built for Anders with no input from him: put relay satellites into real orbits, route signals across the network, and keep the stations talking until dawn.

name: Flutterbloom
desc: A 3D garden grown as a gift for one person — a living sky on her own clock, a meadow that blooms flower by flower, things to build, soft rain and rainbows, and sixteen real butterflies to catch.

name: Bubble Editor
desc: Ballooning an engineering drawing for first-article inspection — drag numbered callouts into place, load your own drawing, export the sheet.

name: The Shop
desc: CNC, G-code and steel — the machines that don't accept an approximately right answer.

name: Frames
desc: Twenty-eight photographs kept as a series. The only thing in the atlas that doesn't do anything — on purpose.

name: Sonic Veil
desc: Composer since 2016 — ambient, experimental and electronic. 86 tracks, ten years of genre-bending, streaming on 150+ platforms.
